name: Vatikan
description: Vatikan is a Russian Rummy variant using double deck + 2 jokers (106 cards). 2-5 players, 13 each. Key feature: players can REARRANGE existing melds on the table to integrate new cards. First meld must be a sequence from hand. Jokers are wild but can't be moved between melds directly. Draw OR meld each turn (not both).

history.origins: Vatikan is described in Andrew Pennycook's A Book of Card Games and is said to be of Central European origin. It belongs to the manipulation rummy family, in which players may rearrange melds on the table; it is very similar to the Italian game Machiavelli and related to Carousel. The tile game Rummikub is a close relative played with tiles rather than cards.
timeline: 20th century: Described in A Book of Card Games; Central European origin.
history.cultural: Popular in Russia and Central Europe; played in the same tradition as Machiavelli and German-style manipulation rummy.
history.evolution: Related to Machiavelli and Carousel; part of the manipulation-rummy family where table melds can be rearranged.

setup.deck: 106 cards (2x52 + 2 jokers). A can be high or low.
setup.dealing: 13 cards each. Remaining cards form the stock; there is no discard pile.

rules.objective: Be the first to get rid of all your cards by melding. There is no scoring; the first player out wins outright.
rules.gameplay: Draw OR meld (not both). Sets (3-4 same rank, different suits) and Runs (3+ sequential same suit). First meld = sequence from hand. REARRANGE existing table melds to add cards. Jokers wild but can't move directly between melds. Replace joker with actual card to free it.
